newsitem.title: UK: International LPG firm as US demand drives market.
newsitem.headline: International LPG firm as US demand drives market.

text.p: International liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices remained strong this week as insatiable U.S. demand remained the dominant factor.
With propane at the main U.S. hub of Mont Belvieu, Texas trading at up to 52 cents a gallon recently, the U.S. has become the market driver for LPG from the Middle East and Europe.
"Demand (in the Middle East Gulf) is coming from everywhere," said a trader. "Everything that shakes free is going to the States."
As a result, premiums to the Saudi Contract Price (CP), against which much Middle Eastern LPG is priced, have risen to at least $15 a tonne on the sellers' side, with buyers not far behind.

Another trader said that as Gulf premiums rise and U.S. demand increases, buyers in Japan and other parts of East Asia were also revising their price ideas upwards. "Basically it's a question of the arbitrage between West and East," he said.
"Premiums for delivered sales to Japan are rising. People are realising that if someone is ready to pay those prices in the West, then Japanese prices have to rise," he added.
